note: Requires both emulators for this task: uv run python server/fakes/gcp.py machine-operating, and STORAGE_EMULATOR_HOST pointing at the running fake-gcs, which the same command brings up. The google-cloud MCP server answers in prose; bq and gcs return JSON. Every google-cloud projection ends in `grep .`, so an arm whose reply carries no such line fails the case instead of agreeing on nothing.

cases.name: list_buckets
cases.why: both arms see the one bucket the seeder made
cases.note: the buckets agree where the datasets do not, because this task's google_cloud_allowed_buckets names the one bucket that exists -- the gap `list_datasets` records is about what each arm can enumerate beyond its scope, and here there is nothing beyond it

cases.name: list_objects_empty
cases.why: an empty bucket reads as empty on both arms rather than erroring on one

mcp.pipe: sed -n 's/^Found \([0-9]*\) objects in bucket.*/\1/p; s/^- //p' | grep .

mirage.pipe: sed -n 's/^Found \([0-9]*\) objects in bucket.*/\1/p; s/^- //p' | grep .

cases.note: the object count proves the reply is a listing rather than an error, and any names that follow are compared too

cases.name: upload_then_list
cases.why: an object written through either arm shows up the same way
cases.note: the two arms send the same bytes by the route each surface offers: the tool takes a host path, the CLI a path under /workspace that the transport maps to the host. `tests/parity.txt` is that file.
